newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets national state debt depository.
newsitem.headline: China sets national state debt depository.

text.p: China said on Friday it had set up a national state debt depository in which all investors and institutions are required to deposit their treasury debt certificates, the Shanghai Securities News said.
The new depository, China Government Securities Depository Trust and Clearing Co, will be responsible for holding, clearing and settling all state debt transactions, the newspaper said.
The depository, jointly established by the Finance Ministry and the People's Bank, the central bank, is aimed at standardising trading procedures and putting a halt to margin trading, it said.
Analysts said its establishment was an important step towards the creation of a national state debt market.

China's state debt market has expanded rapidly in recent years with debt certificates being held and cleared at local depositories attached to each trading centre, the newspaper quoted a Finance Ministry official as saying.

"The lack of a unified depository has made it possible for some institutions to use depository certificates not backed by state debt for margin trading to attract liquidity and even to engage in fraud," the official said.
China's securities rules ban state debt margin trading but many local securities trading centres have allowed the trade with some only maintaining a three percent margin requirement, analysts said.
The illegal margin trading has caused billions of yuan in losses for some state-owned institutions, they said.
"The establishment of the central depository will effectively check margin trading as well as speculative trading," a state debt trader with a major Chinese brokerage said.
Industry sources said the central depository was an important element in Beijing's plans to set up a national state debt market.

The central government wants the STAQ computerised trading system, which now mainly trades institutional (non-public) shares, to take over state debt trading from local markets including the Shanghai stock exchange, sources said.
The Finance Ministry on Friday issued a set of rules governing the new depository, requiring all regional markets to transfer state debt certificates deposited locally to the central depository.
The rules come into effect immediately but industry sources said it would need time for all local markets to transfer state debt certificates in their hands to the central depository.
